newsitem.title: UK: Lonrho delays hotel prospectus, weighs bids.
newsitem.headline: Lonrho delays hotel prospectus, weighs bids.

text.p: British conglomerate Lonrho Plc said on Thursday it had been approached by a number of parties interested in bidding for all or part of its Princess and Metropole hotel groups.
It said that subsequently it had decided to defer publication of its propectus for the hotel groups in order to have sufficient time to evaluate the bid approaches.
Lonrho said on August 12 that it intended to float its booming hotels business within two months as the first step of a planned three-way split of the company's diverse holdings.
It said at the time that a prospectus detailing the float of the Princess and Metropole chains as a separate company would be available in early September with the flotations a month later.
Analysts anticipated proceeds of around 700 million pounds ($1.10 billion).
The Metropole chain has hotels in London, Birmingham and Brighton, southeast England while the 10 Princess hotels are located in the United States, Caribbean and Mexico.

A Lonrho spokesman said the company had received a "variety of bids" from an unspecified number of parties from Britain and overseas for its Princess and Metropole hotels group and expects to make a decision on their future by the end of September.

"The prospectus was due tomorrow but leading up to this we had a variety of approaches which have hardened to such a degree ...as to require a pause in the flotation process," the spokesman said, adding that the bids were not yet down to final figures.
"We had a mixture of bids. We wouldn't want to comment on the identity of the bidders but there is both British and overseas interest and there are hotel groups in there," he said.
He added that some bidders were interested in the whole group and others in parts of it, but declined to say whether the Princess or Metropole chains had attracted more interest.

He said Lonrho expected to issue a clear statement of what would happen next by the end of this month, adding that the options for the hotels group were to continue with flotation as planned or a partial or total "trade sale" (to another hotel group). ($1=.6382 Pound)
